main_issue: Whether Agent D may keep wearing her medical alert bracelet under the new no-visible-jewellery rule (resolved by covering it).

A-B.evidence: B raised the question (turn 2), A answered it (turn 3), and B later said 'Yeah, clear' (15) without objecting to the cover-up compromise.

A-C.evidence: C argued the bracelet is medical, not fashion (5, 7), A insisted on the literal wording (6), then A allowed covering it (9) and C said 'I'm clear' (17).

A-D.evidence: A said it must come off (3), D proposed covering it (8), A agreed 'If we can't see it, that's fine' (9), and D accepted 'will do' (10, 13).

B-C.evidence: B asked about the bracelet (2) and C defended it (5, 7), but neither addressed the other; both later said they were clear (15, 17).

B-D.evidence: B raised D's bracelet (2), D proposed a cover (8), and B later said 'clear' (15); no direct exchange.

C-D.evidence: C defended the bracelet as medical (5, 7), D said she must wear it and proposed covering it (8); C later said 'clear' (17).
